findings.title: XSS via unescaped request.referer in JavaScript context
findings.body: The `request.referer` value is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string literal (`'<%= request.referer %>'`) without any escaping. An attacker who can influence the Referer header (e.g., by embedding the iframe from a page with a crafted URL containing a single quote) can break out of the string and inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the context of the Discourse domain. Use `j` (escape_javascript) or `raw escape_javascript(...)` to sanitize the value.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin validation using indexOf
findings.body: The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` uses substring matching rather than exact comparison. If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, then a malicious origin like `https://forum.example.com.evil.com` would pass the check because it is a substring of `discourseUrl`. This allows a malicious page to send forged `discourse-resize` messages. Use an exact equality check (e.g., compare `e.origin` to the origin portion of `discourseUrl`).

findings.title: Unsanitized raw HTML rendered from external feed content
findings.body: `<%= raw post.cooked %>` outputs the post's cooked content without any HTML sanitization. When `cook_method` is `raw_html` (as set for imported feed content), `Post#cook` returns the raw input directly. This means any `<script>` tags or event handlers present in the RSS/Atom feed content will execute in the user's browser on the Discourse domain, enabling stored XSS. The content should be sanitized (e.g., with the `Sanitize` gem already in the Gemfile) before rendering.

findings.title: String#scrub is not an HTML sanitization method
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` calls `String#scrub` which was introduced in Ruby 2.1 to replace invalid byte sequences in a string's encoding — it does not strip or sanitize HTML tags. This means raw HTML from the feed (including potentially dangerous markup) is passed through to `CGI.unescapeHTML` and then to `TopicEmbed.import` without any tag filtering. If the intent was to strip HTML, a different method should be used; if the intent was to allow HTML, the call is a no-op at best and misleading at worst.

findings.title: embed_url parameter not validated against embeddable_host before enqueuing fetch job
findings.body: The `embed_url` parameter from user input is passed directly to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` without verifying that its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Although `TopicRetriever` performs a host check, the controller should also validate this to avoid enqueuing unnecessary jobs for arbitrary URLs and to provide defense in depth against SSRF if the retriever's check is ever bypassed or changed.

findings.title: Mutating the contents parameter with << causes side effects for callers
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` mutates the string object passed by the caller. In `poll_feed.rb`, `i.content.scrub` returns a new string so it's safe there, but in `import_remote` the `doc.content` result is passed directly. If any caller reuses the string or passes a frozen string, this will raise a `FrozenError` or produce unexpected results. Use `contents = contents + ...` or `contents.dup` before appending.

findings.title: Test expects synchronous TopicRetriever call but controller enqueues a background job
findings.body: The test mocks `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, expecting a synchronous call. However, the controller implementation calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, which enqueues a Sidekiq job rather than calling `TopicRetriever` directly. This test will fail against the actual implementation, meaning the controller's retrieval path is not properly tested.

findings.title: open-uri used to fetch arbitrary URL without redirect restrictions
findings.body: `open(url).read` in `import_remote` uses Ruby's `open-uri` which follows HTTP redirects by default. Even though `TopicRetriever` checks the initial host, a malicious embeddable host could respond with a redirect to an internal network address (e.g., `http://169.254.169.254/` for cloud metadata), enabling SSRF. Consider using a library that restricts redirects or validates the final resolved host.

findings.title: Non-standard ERB syntax 'end if' may cause confusion or errors
findings.body: Line 6 uses `<%- end if %>` which is non-standard ERB. While Ruby may parse `end if` as a valid (albeit unusual) modifier expression, the intent is clearly just `<%- end %>`. This could confuse future maintainers and some ERB processors may not handle it correctly.
